name: Valencia Pectinas S.A.
notes: Incumbent sole source of ING-PEC-450 since 2019 and the origin of the 2024 shortage (post-mortem PM-2024-014). Declared force majeure on 2026-09-02 following a fire in the extraction hall of the Valencia plant. Reliability score downgraded from 0.91 to 0.62 after the second material failure in three years. Contract LAC-PEC-2024-08 contains a force majeure clause that suspends but does not terminate supply obligations. Company indicates a 10-14 week restart, unconfirmed.

name: Rheinland Hydrocolloids GmbH
notes: Fully qualified for ING-PEC-450 since the 2024 emergency spot purchase, so no stage-gate work is required. Price is approximately 18% above the incumbent. Monthly capacity of 40,000 kg covers roughly 55% of group requirement at current run rates and the plant is already committed to other customers until mid-October. Holds a valid EU organic operator certificate, so it can serve organic Naturel and Kids lines. Fastest and lowest-carbon alternative available.

name: Citrus Andina Ltda
notes: Conditionally qualified: gates G1 and G2 closed in March 2026, on-site audit G3 outstanding and estimated at four weeks plus travel. Cheapest EU-landed price at EUR 11.85 per kg but a 55-day sea lead time makes it useless for the first-wave response. Holds no EU organic operator certificate, so it cannot serve organic-labelled SKUs. Strong structural candidate as a permanent second source with a sustainability improvement plan. EUDR geolocation data for citrus feedstock supplied for 71% of collection area.

name: Nanjing Botanical Extracts Co. Ltd
notes: Requires the full G1 to G4 qualification path, estimated at ten weeks, and cannot be compressed below three to four weeks even under an emergency derogation. Lowest price in the panel at EUR 10.40 per kg. No EU organic operator certificate and no third-country equivalence recognition for organic production, so it is excluded from all organic Naturel and Kids SKUs. Sustainability score of 44 falls below the group threshold of 50 and would require executive derogation with a documented improvement plan. Treated as a last-resort option.

name: Coopérative Laitière de l'Ouest
notes: Farmer cooperative supplying the Rennes and Lyon sites on 48-hour collection cycles. Strategic partner since 2011 with an evergreen volume commitment. Highest sustainability score in the panel, driven by pasture-based farming and on-farm biogas.

name: Noord Dairy Ingredients B.V.
notes: Primary source of skimmed milk powder and bovine gelatin for the Bremen and Ghent sites, and secondary source of culture. Gelatin supply carries full TSE/BSE documentation. Reliable but priced at the upper end of the powder market.

name: Great Lakes Starch & Specialties Inc.
notes: Supplies modified waxy maize starch to the Zaragoza site and stevia to Bremen. USD-denominated contract creates FX exposure hedged quarterly. No EU organic certificate; excluded from organic lines.

name: Nordisk Kultur A/S
notes: Sole source of the proprietary YC-X11 starter culture that defines the Lactovia Naturel texture profile. A strain change would require full sensory and shelf-life re-validation, so this is a deliberate strategic single source with a 90-day frozen safety stock held at Ghent.

name: Bremer Zucker & Verpackung GmbH
notes: Bulk beet sugar by silo delivery to Rennes and Bremen, plus printed PP cups and lidding foil. Print-plate changes for new artwork carry a 6-8 week lead time and a EUR 14,000 plate set cost per SKU.

name: Kerala Aromatics Pvt Ltd
notes: Bourbon vanilla extract and steviol glycosides. Vanilla pricing has moved 40% year on year and is hedged with six-month forward purchases. Holds an EU organic operator certificate covering the vanilla range only.
